event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: CMG’s 2021 filing provides abundant, current-period evidence that the COVID-19 pandemic is exerting a material, multi-faceted strain on the company.  The disclosure spans already-incurred impacts (restaurant closures, higher operating costs, reduced guest traffic, delayed capital projects) and forward-looking uncertainties (future supply-chain shortfalls, labour availability, demand recovery timelines).  Language is explicit—using terms such as “has adversely affected,” “materially,” and “could continue”—and ties the pandemic to core financial metrics like liquidity, sales and growth capacity.  Because the filing date (February 2021) sits well within three years of the WHO’s March 2020 declaration, the Time Decay Principle allows high severity scores.  While CMG notes certain mitigating actions (e.g., safety protocols, supplier communication), these are outweighed by the breadth of direct disruptions and the company’s own admission that it cannot forecast the pandemic’s duration or ultimate financial toll.  Overall, the risk profile is acute and ongoing, warranting elevated scores across most extracted sentences.

evidence_list.snippet: The novel coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic has adversely affected and could continue to adversely affect our financial results, operations and outlook for an extended period of time.

components.reason: States a realised adverse effect on financial results.
Projects continued adverse impact into the future.
Covers multiple critical areas (operations and outlook).
Emphasises duration ('extended period of time').

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Directly links COVID-19 to past and future material harm across financial and operational dimensions, justifying a high score of 8.

evidence_list.snippet: The novel coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, and restrictions imposed by federal, state and local governments in response to the outbreak, have disrupted and will continue to disrupt our business.

components.reason: Confirms actual business disruption already occurring.
Signals ongoing disruption ('will continue').
Highlights external government constraints beyond company control.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Explicit evidence of current and future disruption tied to mandatory restrictions merits a score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: In response to the COVID-19 outbreak and government restrictions, we were required to close some of our restaurants, close many of our dining rooms and offer only takeout and delivery, and/or implement modified work hours.

components.reason: Indicates compulsory restaurant and dining-room closures.
Shows operational pivot to take-out/delivery, evidencing disruption.
Mentions modified labour hours, hinting at staffing challenges.
Scope covers multiple restaurants/dining rooms.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Mandatory closures and operational shifts create significant immediate impact, producing a score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: The mobility restrictions, fear of contracting the coronavirus and the sharp increase in unemployment caused by the closure of businesses in response to the COVID-19 outbreak, have adversely affected and will continue to adversely affect our guest traffic, which in turn adversely impacts our liquidity, financial condition or results of operations.

components.reason: Links specific pandemic factors to reduced guest traffic.
Connects traffic decline to liquidity and financial condition.
Projects continued adverse effect ('will continue').
Cites macro drivers (unemployment, fear) amplifying demand risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows cascading demand-side impact on core financial health, yielding a severity score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: Our restaurant operations have been and could continue to be disrupted by employees who are unable or unwilling to work, whether because of illness, quarantine, fear of contracting COVID-19 or caring for family members due to COVID-19 disruptions or illness.

components.reason: Highlights labour shortages already experienced.
Enumerates multiple pandemic-related causes (illness, quarantine, fear, caregiving).
Warns of ongoing future disruption ('could continue').
Directly ties to operational capability.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Labour disruption threatens operations, with a present-and-future lens, warranting a score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: These measures have increased our operating costs and adversely affected our liquidity.

components.reason: Quantifies cost pressure on operations.
Notes negative effect on liquidity.
Contextually tied to pandemic safety measures (implicit mitigation, cost trade-off).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: While the extra safety spend is a mitigation, it materially erodes liquidity, leading to a mid-level score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 outbreak also has affected and may continue to adversely affect the ability of certain of our suppliers to fulfill their obligations to us, which may negatively affect our restaurant operations.

components.reason: Addresses supply-chain impairment already observable.
Signals continuing risk ('may continue').
Connects supplier failure to operational impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concrete mention of vendor shortfalls and operational knock-on effects justifies a score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: If our suppliers are unable to fulfill their obligations to us, we could face shortages of food items or other supplies at our restaurants, and our operations and sales could be adversely impacted.

components.reason: Identifies potential shortages of critical inputs.
Links shortages to adverse operational and sales impact.
Conditional wording indicates risk not yet realised.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking supply risk without current impact moderates the score to 4.

evidence_list.snippet: To preserve liquidity, we delayed new restaurant construction and restaurant remodels that were scheduled to begin during the first half of the year, and we limited restaurant remodels to restaurants that do not have a digital make line or Chipotlane.

components.reason: Shows capital projects deferred due to pandemic pressure.
Direct link to liquidity strain.
Indicates strategic constraint on growth initiatives.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Growth-hindering liquidity-driven delays warrant a moderate risk score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: These changes may materially adversely affect our ability to grow our business, particularly if these construction projects are delayed for a significant amount of time.

components.reason: Explicitly warns of material adverse effect on growth.
Contingent future risk dependent on delay length.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights potential strategic drag; conditional nature keeps score at 4.

evidence_list.snippet: We cannot predict how long the COVID-19 outbreak will last or if it will reoccur even after the vaccines are widely administered, when government restrictions and mandates will be imposed or lifted, or how quickly, if at all, guests will return to their pre-COVID-19 purchasing behaviors, so we cannot predict how long our results of operations and financial performance will be adversely impacted.

components.reason: Emphasises high uncertainty around duration and consumer behaviour.
Directly ties uncertainty to inability to forecast adverse financial impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Open-ended uncertainty across key variables raises concern, yielding a score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: We remain in regular contact with our major suppliers and while to date we have not experienced significant disruptions in our supply chain, we could see future disruptions should the impacts of COVID-19 extend for a considerable amount of time.

components.reason: Acknowledges potential future supply-chain disruptions.
Notes absence of disruptions to date (mitigating).
Mentions proactive communication with suppliers (mitigating).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Current mitigation and lack of realised impact outweigh the forward risk, limiting the score to 1.
